headline: Sensex ends 333 points higher, Nifty crosses 23,200 to snap fall
why: Market snapped a two-day losing streak driven by selective buying in benchmark heavyweights.
US Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 bps to 3.75-4% range for the first time since 2023.
Commerce Ministry proposed a 5-year extension and higher outlay for the RoDTEP export scheme.
whatHappening: Sensex closed 333 points higher while Nifty 50 finished above the 23,200 mark.
Centre hiked the EPFO wage ceiling to ₹25,000 per month after a gap of 12 years.
PM Modi interacted with semiconductor industry leaders ahead of the upcoming Semicon event.
Paytm remained under focus amidst market volatility and opening trade queries.

stocksInNews.sources: Stock in focus during market opening
PM interacts with chip industry ahead of Semicon event
Impact of US Fed 25 bps interest rate hike on IT spending
Broad market rebound helping benchmark indices snap 2-day fall

summary:
Indian benchmark indices snapped a two-day losing streak as the Sensex gained 333 points and Nifty settled above 23,200.
Major developments included the US Fed's 25 bps rate hike, EPFO wage ceiling expansion to ₹25,000, and PM Modi's chip industry push.
